passages.quote: A Chinese agricultural book of the Song dynasty, by Chen Fu, in 3 books. Completed in Shaoxing 19 (1149).
passages.original: 中国，宋代の農書。陳旉の著。3巻。紹興19（1149）年完成。

passages.quote: Book 1 carries 14 chapters on farming, book 2 three chapters on raising oxen and ox medicine, and book 3 five chapters on sericulture, and it is an important source for knowing the wet-rice cultivation methods of the Jiangnan region, ox husbandry, sericulture and more.
passages.original: 上巻は農業 14編，中巻は畜牛，牛医 3編，下巻は養蚕 5編を載せ，江南地方の水稲栽培法，ウシの飼育法，養蚕法などを知るのに重要な文献である。

passages.quote: The method of weeding a field: first examine the lie of the land, and go from the bottom to the top, drying and weeding in turn. First collect and store the water at the topmost place so it is not lost. Then, from the bottom, let each part off to dry and weed it as it dries.
passages.original: 且耘田之法，必先審度形勢，自下及上，旋乾旋耘。先於最上處收滀水，勿致水走失。然後自下旋放令乾而旋耘。

footnotes.assertion: A twelfth-century manual of the lower Yangtze drains the paddies one at a time, from the bottom up, to weed them.Chen Fu's manual, completed in 1149 and a source for the wet rice of Jiangnan, first stores the water at the topmost plot so that none is lost, then lets the plots dry from the bottom up and weeds each as it dries.
footnotes.question: 0009-the-paddy-through-the-rice-year-flooding-draining-transplanting-and-after-the-harvest.html

passages.quote: In making the bund, width is what matters; then the water can be kept at the right depth. If, just after the seed is sown, a sudden wind comes, quickly let the water off, so the waves do not wash the seed and heap it up; if a sudden heavy rain comes, add a little water, since the downpour otherwise floats and tosses the seed and lifts the grain's roots; if it is sunny, keep the water shallow, so the sun can warm it. But shallow must not be too shallow: too shallow and the skin of the mud dries hard. Deep must not be too deep: too deep and the seed is submerged, soaked to the heart, and wilts and yellows.
passages.original: 作堘貴闊，則約水深淺得宜。若纔撒種子，忽暴風，卻急放乾水，免風浪淘蕩，聚郤穀也；忽大雨，必稍增水，為暴雨漂颭，浮起穀根也；若晴，卽淺水，從其曬暖也。然淺不可太淺，太淺卽泥皮乾堅。深不可太深，太深卽浸沒沁心而萎黄矣。

footnotes.assertion: The same manual keeps a new seedbed's water shallow in sunshine, so the sun warms it.Not so shallow that the skin of the mud dries hard, nor so deep that the seed is soaked through and yellows; he adds a little water in a downpour, lets it off in a sudden wind, and says a wide bund is what lets the depth be kept right.
footnotes.question: 0009-the-paddy-through-the-rice-year-flooding-draining-transplanting-and-after-the-harvest.html

passages.quote: Doyoboshi of the paddy is also called nakaboshi and the like
passages.original: 水田の土用干しは中干しなどともいい

passages.quote: in farming, draining the water from the paddy around the summer doyo, done to make the rice strong against wind and to make the ears fill well
passages.original: 農業においては夏の土用のころ田（水田）の水を抜き、風に強く、穂をよく実らせるために行うこと

passages.quote: It differs by region, but about one week is the guide.
passages.original: 地域によっても違うがおよそ一週間が目安。

footnotes.assertion: It is also called doyoboshi, drying at the summer doyo.The water is let out of the paddy to make the rice stand up to the wind and fill its ears.

passages.quote: Nagata (1964) examined the irrigation methods recorded in the "Outline of paddy and upland rice cultivation (Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, Agricultural Affairs Bureau, 1933)" and showed that nakaboshi (doyoboshi in the original) was carried out in 22 prefectures. However, before the war its spread was limited to some regions with plentiful water (Tanaka, 1970).
passages.original: 永田（1964）は「水稲及陸稲耕種要綱（農林省農務局，1933）」に記載されている灌漑方法を検討し，22県で中干し（原文では土用干し）が実施されていることを示した。但し，戦前にはその普及は用水の豊富な一部の地方に限られていた（田中，1970）。

passages.quote: Among farm households of the Meiji, Taisho and early Showa periods, a life in keeping with the natural environment was the norm.

passages.quote: There are historical records showing double cropping in the mid-Heian period, and in the Kamakura period it spread fairly widely.
passages.original: 平安時代中期に二毛作の存在を示す史料があり，鎌倉時代には二毛作がかなり普及した。

passages.quote: is clear also from the law of the fourth month of 1264 (Bun'ei 1), by which the Kamakura shogunate ordered the provinces to forbid collecting annual tax on back-crop barley (Shinpen Tsuika).
passages.original: 1264年（文永1）4月に鎌倉幕府が諸国に令して裏作麦の年貢徴収を禁じた法令（《新編追加》）からも明らかである。

footnotes.assertion: The rice-and-barley year is old: recorded from the middle of the Heian period, and fairly widespread by the Kamakura period.In 1264 the Kamakura shogunate ordered the provinces not to tax the winter barley.
footnotes.question: 0009-the-paddy-through-the-rice-year-flooding-draining-transplanting-and-after-the-harvest.html

passages.quote: In the Edo period, as the small holding of the independent farmer became general and farming grew more intensive, the range of paddy double cropping widened further, centered especially on Kinki and San'yo, which were favored with conditions such as improved varieties, purchased fertilizer and irrigation works
passages.original: 江戸時代に入り，本百姓の小規模経営が一般的に成立し，農業経営の集約化が進むと，とくに品種改良，購入肥料，灌漑用水施設などの諸条件に恵まれた近畿や山陽方面を中心として，水田二毛作の範囲がいっそう拡大され

footnotes.assertion: In the Edo period it spread further, above all around Kyoto and Osaka and along the Inland Sea coast west of them.There better seed, bought fertilizer and irrigation works came together.
footnotes.question: 0009-the-paddy-through-the-rice-year-flooding-draining-transplanting-and-after-the-harvest.html

passages.quote: Before World War II, the line joining northern Kanto to Toyama Prefecture was the limit line of rice-barley double cropping; north of it, low temperature, snow cover and wet paddies were the limiting factors on double cropping.
passages.original: 第2次大戦前は北関東から富山県を結ぶ線が米麦二毛作限界線であり，これ以北では低温，積雪および湿田が二毛作の限定要因となっていた。

footnotes.assertion: Before the Second World War the rice-and-barley year stopped at a line across central Japan, from the north of the Kanto plain to Toyama on the Sea of Japan coast.North of it, cold, snow and wet paddies stood in the way.
footnotes.question: 0009-the-paddy-through-the-rice-year-flooding-draining-transplanting-and-after-the-harvest.html

passages.quote: Nanohana (nabana) is sown in autumn; seedlings with 5 to 6 true leaves are set out permanently at a spacing of 30 to 40 centimeters (cm) between plants, are carried through the winter, and are harvested from early March to early April by cutting the flower stalks.
passages.original: 菜の花（ナバナ）は、秋に種をまき、本葉が5 - 6枚の苗を株間30 - 40センチメートル (cm) で定植し、冬を越して3月上旬から4月上旬に花茎を切って収穫する

footnotes.assertion: Rape grown for its flower shoots is sown in autumn and cut in early spring.Rape grown for its flower shoots, nanohana, is sown in autumn, carried through the winter, and its flower stalks cut from early March to early April.
footnotes.question: 0009-the-paddy-through-the-rice-year-flooding-draining-transplanting-and-after-the-harvest.html

passages.quote: In Taiwan, every year after the second-crop rice is harvested before the onset of winter, some rice farmers scatter rape seed on the paddy fields, so that the fields grow full of rape and go on to flower, and before the next year's rice transplanting it is worked into the soil as green manure.
passages.original: 在台灣，每年入冬前第二期水稻收割之後，有些稻農會在稻田灑油菜的種子，使稻田長滿油菜、進而開花，次年水稻插秧前再打入土壤裡做為綠肥。

footnotes.assertion: In Taiwan some rice farmers sow rape on the paddy after the rice, as green manure.They scatter its seed after the second rice crop is cut, and plow it in before the next year's rice is transplanted.
footnotes.question: 0009-the-paddy-through-the-rice-year-flooding-draining-transplanting-and-after-the-harvest.html

passages.quote: In the southern Jiangxi region (that is, Ganzhou) the rape harvest time is the first ten days of April, in Jiujiang it is the first ten days of May, and in other regions the middle and last ten days of April; in most of southern Jiangxi the rice transplanting time is the middle ten days of April, and in most of northern and central Jiangxi it is the last ten days of April to the first ten days of May.
passages.original: 赣南地区(即赣州)油菜收获时间为4月上旬, 九江为5月上旬, 其他地区为4月中下旬; 赣南大部分地区水稻移栽时间为4月中旬, 赣北赣中大部为4月下旬—5月上旬。

footnotes.assertion: In Jiangxi, in southern China, the rape today comes off in April or early May, just as the rice goes in.The same page gives no month for the rice harvest.
